result.headline: No-hint DQN reached a test mean of 20.36 (seed group 20.67 ± 0.46), and both hints scored only about 0.5–0.7 higher, which is within seed noise.
result.summary:
**No hint (this run, seed 0):** DQN with short vision and the score-only reward (apple +10, death −10) reached a test mean of **20.36 apples-worth of food per game** (median 21, max 40). Across its three seeds the mean is 20.67 with a standard deviation of 0.46. Each test game took about 168 steps and 8 steps per apple, and the snake never starved. Of 100 games, 82 ended by hitting its own body and 18 by hitting a wall. The training mean over the last 100 games was 16.92. That number is lower than the test score because it includes random exploration moves, while the test uses the greedy (always best-guess) policy.

**Learning curve:** The training mean rose quickly and then flattened. It was 15.52 at 0.9 minutes and stayed between 14.7 and 16.8 for the rest of the 10 minutes, while the best single game only moved from 38 to 45. Steps per second fell from about 6,600 at the start to about 3,600–4,300 later, which is normal for a run sharing the machine. The curves in this run are for seed 0 only, so this run alone cannot show which hint learned fastest early on.

**Hints, judged against the seed spread:** Distance hint: 21.22 mean (21.68, 21.16, 20.82). Potential hint: 21.38 mean (21.61, 20.69, 21.84). That is about +0.5 and +0.7 over no hint, but the gap is about 1.5 times the seed spread, so with three seeds per group it is not a reliable difference. The hints also did not change how games ended: wall and body crashes stayed about the same, and none starved.
result.diagnosis:
The curve reaches its plateau within about one minute and stays there for nine more. That points to a ceiling set by the information the agent receives, not by how long it trains. Short vision only sees the next square, so the snake cannot tell that a long body is about to trap its head. This explains why 82% of deaths are self-collisions. Doubling training time would probably not help much.

Hints add guidance, not information. The potential-based hint is designed so it cannot change the best strategy, and a 0.1 distance hint is small next to the apple reward of 10, so neither can lift the ceiling much. The small gains we see are most likely seed noise. The spread across seeds (0.46) is about the same size as the hint effects, so one run cannot separate them.
result.learned: A hint can change how fast an agent learns, but it cannot give the agent information it does not have. When the learning curve plateaus early, check the vision and the seed spread before blaming the reward or the training time.

recommendations.title: Give the snake rays to see further
recommendations.why: The plateau at about 15–17 training points after one minute suggests the short vision is the ceiling. Testing rays with depth 4 checks whether seeing further lifts the score.
recommendations.change: Switch the vision from short to rays (depth 4), keeping the score-only reward and the 10-minute budget.
recommendations.prediction: Test mean rises from about 20.4 to roughly 23–27, and the share of body crashes falls below 70%.
recommendations.question: Does seeing further raise the ceiling that the hints could not move?

recommendations.title: Make the distance hint too loud
recommendations.why: The lesson's Try-this asks whether a large hint makes the snake chase the hint instead of the apple. A weight of 1.0 is ten times the 0.1 hint and tests that directly.
recommendations.change: Add a distance reward of 1.0 to the no-hint score reward, keeping everything else the same.
recommendations.prediction: Test mean drops below 20 and steps per apple rise above 8, because the snake takes longer routes toward the hint.
recommendations.question: At what hint size does distance guidance start to hurt rather than help?

recommendations.title: Train for 30 minutes to check the plateau
recommendations.why: If the plateau were just slow learning, a longer run would keep improving. Tripling the budget tests that.
recommendations.change: Increase the time budget from 10 to 30 minutes, keeping the same recipe and seed.
recommendations.prediction: Test mean stays within about 1 point of 20.4, because the curve is already flat from minute 1 to minute 10.
recommendations.question: Is the score limited by training time, or by what the agent can see?

ideas.title: Early-learning speed score per run
ideas.what: Report the average training score over the first few minutes, or the environment steps needed to reach a set score, for each run. Show it next to the final test score in seed-group comparisons.
ideas.why: The lesson asks which hint helps most early on, but the final test scores differ by less than the seed spread, and the early comparison needs one number per run. This run's curve shows the plateau is reached within about one minute, so the early phase is where hints would matter.
ideas.expected: Would separate hint groups by learning speed, for example showing whether a hint reaches a training mean of 15 in fewer env steps, and makes the early-phase comparison readable without eyeballing curves.
